Default age grid

Source: R/build_inputs.R
default_age_lower.Rd

Lower edges, in years, of the default age groups: fine in childhood, where immunity and maternal immunity change fast, and coarse in adulthood.

Usage

default_age_lower(max_age = 80, n_group = 118L)

Arguments

max_age

lower edge, in years, of the oldest age group, which is open-ended. A single finite number of at least 20: below that the grid has too few anchors left to resolve the ages over which immunity develops.

n_group

total number of age groups, the open-ended top group included. A whole number of at most 1e6, and at least one more than the number of anchor intervals below max_age (14 for max_age = 80). Changing it refines or coarsens the whole grid while keeping its shape, as a grid-convergence check needs; run time is roughly proportional to it.

Value

A numeric vector of age-group lower edges in years, from 0 to max_age.

Details

Group edges are pinned at the conventional reporting ages, 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40 and 60 years, so that the usual output bands fall on group boundaries, and at 21, so that whole groups make up the year, [20, 21), from which the IBM draws maternal immunity. Groups between two anchors are of equal width. The groups are shared among the anchor intervals in proportion to each interval's width in log(1 + age), weighted 1.25 below 5 years and 0.5 from 21 years; each interval gets at least one group, and the remainder is allocated by largest remainder.

The width is logarithmic because what the grid has to resolve is the rise of immunity with age, which is far closer to a function of log age than of age. (log(1 + age) rather than log(age), which is infinite over the first year; the offset is in years, so the allocation is not scale-free.) The grading matters more than the count: at 53 groups an equal-width grid is four times as far from the converged solution as a log-graded one (rms over the age profile), and a grid of fixed monthly, quarterly, yearly and 5-yearly sections, which over-resolves infancy and under-resolves everything above 15, 1.7 times as far. The grid's error is largest in clinical and severe incidence among young children at high transmission; each age band's error comes from the groups inside it, and the groups above 21 years have no measurable effect on any child's incidence. The weights move groups to where the error arises, and match the unweighted grid's accuracy with about a quarter fewer groups.

The default, 118 groups, is the smallest grid on which every falciparum claim in fleetcheck passes, not the most accurate; the deciding claim is the clinical age profile's 3-5 year band at EIR 120, which needs 14 groups between 3 and 5 years. fleet's age profile converges at first order: its departure from the converged profile is fleet-low and halves with each doubling of n_group. On the default grid the largest departure of the EIR 20 clinical age profile is 3.2%, in the oldest band, which the weights coarsen, and the rms 1.6%; on 53 groups they are 6.1% and 3.2%. Against the IBM median, severe incidence at EIR 120 is 2% low on the default grid and 7% low on 53 groups.

n_group = 53 runs over twice as fast and is adequate where a result does not rest on the level of severe incidence, or of young children's incidence at high transmission; n_group = 236 halves the grid's error for twice the cost. Refinement does not remove the mean-field approximation itself, one immunity value per stratum where the IBM holds a spread of infection histories at the same age, so a persistent difference from the IBM is not evidence that the grid is too coarse. fleetcheck measures both, in validations/age-grid/run.R and the age-profile-clinical and severe-allage-eir claims.

Output bands and intervention age targets that do not fall on a group edge are apportioned by the fraction of each group's width they cover; neither is snapped to the grid.

See also

ode_tuning(), which takes the grid as age_lower.
